source_rule: Narrative facts are extracted only from the chapter source files in data/source. External sources are not used to invent narrative facts.

events.description: Takezo is wounded and left among the dead after the Battle of Sekigahara; the chapter recounts the collapse of the Western Army.
Takezo discovers that Matahachi survived and the two reunite on the battlefield.
The two leave the battlefield and spend two days foraging in the Mount Ibuki area.
They travel in what they believe is the direction of Tarui; the text does not establish an arrival in Tarui before the next refuge scene.
Akemi and Oko shelter the two sick stragglers in their mountain house.
Akemi reveals that her family makes and sells moxa and that patrols remain active after Sekigahara.
Takezo goes mushroom hunting in the mountain with Akemi.
Tsujikaze Temma confronts Akemi and demands a share of her family's illicit earnings.
Akemi admits that she scavenges battlefields for valuables and says Temma is believed to have killed her father.
Temma and his men raid the house; Takezo and Matahachi resist them.
Takezo pursues Temma and kills him with the wooden sword.
The final scene establishes that Oko, Akemi and Matahachi have left the refuge together; their destination is not established. Takezo remains behind and discovers the empty house.
The narrative shifts to Miyamoto, where Otsu lives at Shippoji and Takuan is staying at the temple.
Otsu and Takuan walk down to the Aida River to gather flowers for the festival.
Otsu and Takuan go to Ogin's house to collect Otsu's festival obi.
Otsu meets Ogin and learns that the family believes Takezo and Matahachi died at Sekigahara.
Otsu sees Takezo in the crowd during the flower festival; he immediately disappears to avoid capture.
Osugi learns that Takezo has been seen and the Himeji garrison begins an intensified search.
Takezo repeatedly evades the Himeji soldiers and hides in the Sanumo Mountains.
Himeji soldiers raid Ogin's house and arrest her. A villager later reports only a rumor that she is held at Hinagura, so arrival there is not yet confirmed. Otsu witnesses the arrest and escapes.
Takezo secretly tells Osugi that Matahachi is alive and asks her to pass the news to Otsu.
Osugi deceives Takezo into taking a bath while a group of soldiers and villagers surround the house; Takezo escapes.
Otsu receives letters from Oko and Matahachi explaining that Matahachi is alive in another province and intends to marry Oko.
Takuan takes Otsu into the mountains and chooses Itadori Pasture as their camp.
Takezo approaches their camp after hearing Otsu's flute and is persuaded to come to the fire.
Takuan subdues Takezo psychologically and ties him up, completing the promised capture.
Takuan brings the captured Takezo back to Shippoji, and Otsu returns to the temple from the mountain camp.
Takezo is tied to the old cryptomeria tree and the villagers demand punishment; Takuan retains authority over his fate.
Otsu increasingly identifies with Takezo's suffering and begins actively seeking his survival.
Otsu climbs the tree, cuts Takezo free and escapes with him through the mountains.
At Nakayama Pass, Takezo decides to rescue Ogin while Otsu agrees to continue toward Himeji and wait at Hanada Bridge.
Otsu travels alone toward Himeji, becomes ill and collapses at the Mikazuki Teahouse.
Osugi and Gonroku discover Otsu at the teahouse and pursue her; she escapes by diving into a ravine. The later recovery is deferred to chapter 8.
Takezo studies the Hinagura stockade and attacks it to rescue Ogin.
Takezo learns that Ogin was moved to Himeji before his assault.
After escaping the stockade, Takezo heads toward Himeji.
Takezo waits around Himeji, including under and on Hanada Bridge, while trying to locate Ogin.
Takuan finds Takezo and brings him into Himeji Castle.
Takezo appears before Ikeda Terumasa, who accepts Takuan's proposed form of punishment and confinement.
Takezo remains confined in the castle's dark chamber for approximately three years, studying and reflecting.
After three years, Takuan returns and Takezo is released from confinement.
Takezo is renamed Miyamoto Musashi and rejects immediate service as a vassal, choosing to travel independently.
Takuan reports the later whereabouts of Ogin, the continued search by Osugi and Gonroku, and Aoki Tanzaemon's dismissal from Ikeda's service.
Musashi meets Otsu, who has waited for him for three years at Hanada Bridge.
Musashi refuses to take Otsu with him and leaves alone toward the east after leaving her a farewell message.
Seijuro, Toji, Ryohei and the Yoshioka students leave the school for the Kamo River pleasure district.
The Yoshioka group drinks, sings and argues in a pleasure-district house.
Toji and Ryohei separate two students after a fight.
Seijuro leaves the first establishment and Toji follows him to Yomogi while Ryohei remains with the students.
Seijuro and Toji arrive at Yomogi, where Oko and Akemi receive them.
Toji and Oko negotiate privately at Yomogi.
Seijuro drinks and flirts with Akemi at Yomogi.
Oko and Matahachi argue about their marriage while Matahachi remains isolated in a back room.
Akemi interacts with Matahachi within the Yomogi household.
Musashi enters the Yoshioka School after accepting its challenge.
Musashi defeats successive Yoshioka challengers; several disciples are wounded and two later die.
Seijuro and Toji return to the school and assess the aftermath of Musashi's bouts.
Seijuro, Toji, Ryohei and senior disciples deliberate on how to deal with Musashi.
The Yoshioka group attempts a night ambush in Musashi's assigned room.
Musashi escapes through the floorboards and leaves the school by an unestablished route.
Yoshioka pursuers leave the back gate and chase a fleeing figure toward the burned Honnōji ruins.
The pursuers capture Matahachi near Honnōji, mistaking him for Musashi.
Toji recognizes Matahachi from Yomogi and the pursuers discover their error.
Left by the Honnōji moat, Matahachi recognizes Musashi's new name and resolves to warn him.
Denshichiro is reported absent in Ise; this report does not place him physically at the Yoshioka School.
Musashi observes potters in the ceramic district on the road below Kiyomizudera.
Musashi climbs to the Kiyomizudera grounds and stops at a cliff overlooking Kyoto.
A palanquin bearer identifies Musashi and carries the information back toward Chawan Hill.
Porters surround Musashi on the approach to Hongando.
Osugi and Gonroku arrive at Hongando and confront Musashi.
Musashi refuses the family revenge confrontation and walks through the crowd without fighting Osugi or Gonroku.
The crowd searches the Kiyomizudera hills until sunset while Musashi escapes through the wider area.
Jotaro visits the innkeeper at a cheap inn northwest of Kyoto.
Musashi returns to the inn and talks with Jotaro in the hearth room.
Jotaro writes the innkeeper's letter and handles it for Musashi.
Jotaro works at the sake shop, where Matahachi later gives him a letter for Musashi.
Musashi leaves the inn toward Nara and Jotaro follows him.
Musashi passes the Sanjo Avenue security checkpoint.
Musashi and Jotaro reunite on the Daigo mountain road after Jotaro's pursuit.
Musashi and Jotaro stop at Rokuamida, where Musashi writes to Seijuro.
Jotaro turns back toward Kyoto while Musashi continues toward Nara; neither arrival occurs in this event.
Jotaro receives Matahachi's letter for Musashi; no physical meeting between the two men occurs.
Jotaro meets Akemi in the Takase River and Yomogi area and asks about Matahachi.
Jotaro delivers Musashi's message at Yomogi and learns that Matahachi has left.
Jotaro travels south on the Yamato highroad by ox cart toward Mampukuji.
Jotaro loses his bamboo tube near Mampukuji and Otsu helps identify it.
Kizaemon returns Jotaro's lost bamboo tube.
Jotaro, Otsu and Kizaemon travel together toward Uji.
The trio rests at a Uji Bridge teahouse while Kizaemon discusses conditions in Nara with its proprietor.
Otsu chooses the Koyagyu route with Kizaemon while Jotaro continues toward Nara.
Jotaro separates from Otsu and Kizaemon at the Kizu River ferry.
Musashi searches the Abura Hill and Ozoin vicinity for Hozoin.
A young monk directs Musashi through Ozoin toward Hozoin.
Musashi meets Nikkan in the Ozoin garden and is affected by the abbot's spiritual pressure.
Musashi registers at Hozoin as a visiting student.
Musashi watches Agon and the other Hozoin students train in the dojo.
Musashi fights Agon on the dojo floor and kills him.
Nikkan speaks privately with Musashi and explains the lesson about his excessive fighting spirit.
Musashi leaves Hozoin, briefly returns to leave instructions for Jotaro, then proceeds toward Sarusawa Pond.
Musashi takes lodging at a boardinghouse near Sarusawa Pond.
Dampachi, Banryu and Yasubei try to recruit Musashi for public matches, but he refuses.
Jotaro arrives at the Sarusawa boardinghouse with the Yoshioka response and reunites with Musashi.
Inshun is absent during Musashi's initial Hozoin visit; no physical presence is inferred.
Musashi and Jotaro travel from Nara through the Todaiji area toward Hannya Plain.
Musashi positions Jotaro on a nearby knoll to observe the wider Hannya Plain scene.
Musashi recognizes Dampachi's trap and kills him on Hannya Plain.
Hozoin priests and ronin, including Banryu and Yasubei, are encamped around a bonfire.
Musashi fights the ronin group and kills several of its members.
Inshun leads the Hozoin priests in the deliberate purge of the remaining ronin, including Banryu and Yasubei.
Nikkan arrives with five government officials, who inspect the bodies after the battle.
Nikkan explains the purge, advises Musashi and involves Jotaro in rites for the dead.
Jotaro runs from the observation knoll toward Musashi when the Hozoin charge begins.
About ten days after Hannya Plain, Musashi and Jotaro arrive in Yagyu Valley.
Musashi and Jotaro tour the valley and inspect the exterior of Koyagyu Castle.
At Wataya, Jotaro meets Kocha and their teasing becomes a playful physical quarrel.
Musashi bathes with three Kyoto visitors; the narrative identifies Denshichiro among them through Musashi's recognition, but no direct interaction follows.
Musashi, Jotaro and Kocha interact at the inn after the children's quarrel.
Musashi decides to seek a test against the Yagyu name.
Kizaemon's earlier visit to the Kyoto guests is reported in the bath conversation and is not treated as present co-location.
Sekishusai and Otsu discuss flower arrangement and life at the mountain house.
Kizaemon returns from his errand and reports at the mountain-house entrance.
Kizaemon reports delivering the Yagyu response to Denshichiro's party and receives further instructions.
Sekishusai decides to send Otsu to Wataya with a letter and peony instead of receiving Denshichiro.
Otsu rides from the Yagyu estate to Wataya.
Otsu meets Kocha at Wataya and asks for Denshichiro.
Otsu delivers Sekishusai's letter and peony directly to Denshichiro.
Musashi examines the peony stem, reproduces its cut and recognizes the work of an exceptional swordsman.
Otsu rides back toward Koyagyu and encounters Jotaro near the castle and river area.
Jotaro returns to Wataya and gives Musashi Kizaemon's reply letter; Kizaemon is not physically present.
Kocha tends Jotaro's wounds at the inn and stream.
Jotaro and Kocha interact privately in the fodder shed until Kocha's unnamed father interrupts them.
Musashi and Jotaro depart Wataya after Jotaro briefly remains behind to say farewell to Kocha.
Musashi and Jotaro arrive at the main gate of Koyagyu Castle.
Musashi is admitted and taken to Shin'indo while Jotaro is left in the attendants' waiting room.
Kizaemon enters Shin'indo with Kimura, Debuchi and Murata and receives Musashi.
The four Yagyu retainers question and test Musashi during the sake and conversation sequence.
Musashi challenges the hosts to a sword test and they decline to provoke the encounter.
Taro's unusual barking causes Debuchi, then Murata and Kimura, to leave Shin'indo.
Kizaemon learns Jotaro is missing and goes with Musashi toward the disturbance.
Musashi and Kizaemon reach the crowd where Jotaro stands beside the dead dog Taro.
The dog's unnamed keeper attacks Jotaro and Musashi intervenes to protect him.
Musashi challenges the surrounding Yagyu personnel on Jotaro's behalf.
Kizaemon assumes responsibility and orders the crowd to disperse.
Debuchi proposes that Musashi commit suicide and Musashi refuses.
Kimura orders Musashi toward the cells; Musashi instead walks toward the keep and tells Jotaro to wait under a pine in the garden.
Kizaemon and Debuchi try to pull Musashi back while Kimura begins to draw his sword and is restrained.
Musashi declares that he intends to see Sekishusai and challenges the castle to battle.
Kimura accepts the challenge while the senior retainers position themselves around Musashi and Jotaro remains nearby.
Jotaro throws sand to disrupt Kimura's initial sword strike while Musashi evades.
Musashi and Kimura enter a direct sword confrontation while Kizaemon, Debuchi and Murata take positions around them.
Kizaemon, Debuchi and Murata move in together against Musashi.
Otsu's distant flute affects Musashi during the fight; she is not physically present in the castle scene.
Musashi escapes from the castle grounds toward the inner moat and outer darkness; Jotaro is not assumed to remain with him.
Musashi hides by the inner moat after escaping the four retainers.
Musashi searches through the castle woods and valleys for Sekishusai's mountain house.
Musashi reaches the mountain-house gate, reads its plaques and chooses not to enter; no face-to-face meeting with Sekishusai occurs.
Musashi leaves the mountain-house gate and flees toward the wooded Tsukigase-Iga back road.
Otsu and Jotaro search for Musashi on the back road and meet Takuan; Jotaro later turns back for his mask while Otsu and Takuan part.
Matahachi works at the Fushimi Castle construction site and becomes ill.
The traveler kills an inspector and is then fatally attacked by the laborers and guards.
Matahachi takes the dead traveler's bundle, money and sword-school certificate.
Matahachi flees and takes shelter in an abandoned Fushimi house.
He reads a certificate addressed to Sasaki Kojirō; the text does not establish that the dead bearer was Kojirō.
Matahachi and the mendicant priest fight over food; the priest nearly gives the Aoki name and describes his Himeji background.
Matahachi leaves Fushimi to seek information in Osaka.
Matahachi claims the name Sasaki Kojirō; Yasoma flatters and swindles him.
After a gambling fight and flight into a tiger show, Matahachi reunites with Osugi and Gonroku.
Osugi accepts Matahachi's swordsmanship claims and draws him into her revenge plan against Musashi and Otsū.
A passenger ship crosses the Inland Sea from Awa toward Osaka.
The handsome young man describes his training lineage, Iwakuni home, Drying Pole and intended equinox meeting with Tenki; his canonical identity is not yet disclosed.
The handsome young man cuts off Tōji's topknot during their confrontation.
After the monkey steals playing cards, the handsome young man deflects the captain's musket barrel and prevents the shot from striking it.
The ship reaches Kizugawa harbor and the handsome young man disembarks separately.
Tōji rejoins the Yoshioka party at a Sumiyoshi inn and his missing topknot becomes visible.
Akemi searches symbolically for a seashell of forgetfulness on the Sumiyoshi shore.
Seijūrō isolates and sexually assaults Akemi; she escapes the room afterward.
Osugi, Matahachi and Gonroku tour the shrine precincts; Matahachi quarrels and leaves.
Akemi walks into the sea intending to die; Gonroku rescues her but drowns.
Fishermen revive Akemi and Seijūrō tends her fever at the inn.
Ryōhei delivers Musashi's challenge; Seijūrō takes his horse and rides toward Kyoto.
Seven Yoshioka disciples trace Kojirō to the last upstream boat and pursue him toward Kema.
Kojirō lands to meet the challenge and kills multiple disciples; three survivors later bury the dead.
Ryōhei attacks Kojirō and falls; Seijūrō recognizes Ganryū and defuses the confrontation.
The parties become outwardly friendly and continue toward Kyoto; the Yoshioka school is the intended destination.
Musashi travels through Yokkaichi toward Kameyama/Ujii while a foot injury worsens.
Musashi seeks Baiken, meets the household, examines the chain-and-sickle weapon and sleeps at the smithy.
Musashi reaches Yamada, seeks Baiken again and approaches the Inner Shrine as infection worsens.
After purification in the Isuzu River and leaving his swords at the House of Virgins, Musashi climbs Eagle Mountain; the abscess drains at the summit.
Otsū and Jōtarō encounter Musashi's pack and swords but do not securely identify them as his.
After gossip about Otsū's chastity, Ujitomi dismisses her from the House of Virgins.
Ujitomi entrusts painted scrolls to Otsū for delivery to Karasumaru Mitsuhiro in Kyoto.
A servant reports that Musashi's belongings were released to an unidentified claimant against a receipt.
Otsū and Jōtarō pay respects and depart Ise for Kyoto with the scroll box; the Karasumaru residence remains an intended destination.
With his foot healed, Musashi ferries to Ōminato and boards a boat to Tsu; arrival at Tsu is not shown in this event.
Musashi follows Baiken to the smithy; the narration explicitly identifies Baiken as Tsujikaze Kōhei.
Kōhei plies Musashi with drink and stages a night ambush; Musashi hides inside the house while attackers search the roads.
Musashi leaves the wrapped chain-and-sickle at Kōhei's neck instead of killing him, then departs for an unstated destination.
Otsū and Jōtarō rent a horse and continue toward Kyoto through the Suzuka–Ōmi corridor; the Karasumaru residence remains an intended destination.
Baiken tries to seize the horse; Otsū cuts two fingertips while drawing his sword, the wounded horse bolts with Jōtarō, and Baiken's men bind and take Otsū toward an unstated destination.
Jōtarō escapes the runaway horse by grabbing a tree branch, falls unharmed, and runs back searching for Otsū.
Sannojō deceives the henchmen with a false Musashi ambush story; Jōtarō frees Otsū and Sannojō guides them onward.
They reach Kyoto and continue toward the Karasumaru residence to deliver the scrolls; arrival at the residence is not shown.
Akemi slips away from the Sumiyoshi inn and travels by boat up the Yodo toward Kyoto.
Yasoma attacks Akemi; Tanzaemon knocks him unconscious and shelters her in a ruined temple.
Akemi tells Tanzaemon about Seijūrō's assault.
During a falcon hunt, Kojirō tracks a dog to the temple, kills it after it bites Akemi, treats her wound and carries her away toward an unstated destination.
The Yoshioka school schedules the duel for the ninth day of the first month at Rendaiji and posts the announcement at Gojō Bridge.
Musashi finds his aunt and uncle but receives a hostile reception shaped by Osugi's accusations.
Musashi leaves around midnight/New Year and reaches the Kamo River, where he eats rice cakes and bathes.
Osugi attacks with sword and blow needles; Musashi disarms her, carries her to a boat and ties her there to await Matahachi.
Musashi reads the posted Rendaiji duel announcement and recovers Osugi's blow needles.
Akemi meets Musashi and discloses Seijūrō's assault and her feelings; Jōtarō observes while Otsū hides behind an oxcart.
Musashi and the real Kojirō see and assess one another; Musashi sends Akemi back with Kojirō toward the Zuzuya Inn.
Musashi frees Osugi and crosses the Kamo; Otsū and Jōtarō chase while Osugi pursues them.
Osugi persuades Otsū to seek Matahachi with her; Jōtarō plans to return to the Karasumaru house, and they see the duel notice again.
Jōtarō searches among the waiting Yoshioka men for Otsū.
Kojirō and Akemi reach the withered field after Akemi's attempted escape.
Tamihachi reports that Musashi shattered Seijūrō's right shoulder with one wooden-sword blow in the adjacent field.
At Seijūrō's request Kojirō amputates the irreparably injured right arm.
The Yoshioka party carries Seijūrō away from the field toward the Shijō school and a doctor; arrival is not shown.
Musashi leaves the duel field, troubled by victory and its consequences.
Musashi encounters Myōshū and Kōetsu at an outdoor tea picnic beside a brook.
Kōetsu's tea bowl, manner and account of the Hon’ami arts broaden Musashi's idea of mastery.
Myōshū and Kōetsu invite Musashi to visit their Hon’ami Lane home; he does not accept a stay in this chapter.
Matahachi drinks without money, wounds two men and claims the name Sasaki Kojirō.
Gempachi recognizes Tenki's pillbox and pursues Matahachi across Kyoto's southern avenues.
At Matsubara, Matahachi meets Akemi fleeing the real Kojirō and repeats the false identity.
Kojirō identifies himself and his Ganryū name, then knocks the impostor unconscious.
Gempachi recovers Tenki's pillbox and certificate from Matahachi.
Kojirō prevents Gempachi from killing Matahachi and refuses Jisai's certificate.
Gempachi leaves intending to return to Kōzuke; Matahachi remains tied to a tree with an impostor notice while Akemi has escaped again.
Denshichirō returns to Kyoto from travel through Ise, Yamato and Osaka.
Denshichirō cuts Matahachi free from the tree.
Seijūrō cedes the Yoshioka house and school to Denshichirō and warns him not to fight Musashi.
Denshichirō rejects restraint; Nampo Yoichibei leaves the school rather than support revenge.
After learning Musashi is staying with Kōetsu, Denshichirō prepares a formal challenge.
Seijūrō leaves a long letter and disappears from the school.
Osugi keeps Otsū under coercive control at the Sannen Hill inn; Akemi arrives at the same inn.
A priest delivers Matahachi's letter and Osugi takes Otsū to the mountain-god hall at night.
Kojirō, still searching for Akemi, crosses the group's path.
Otsū rejects Matahachi and explicitly affirms her love for Musashi.
Matahachi repeatedly strikes a body in the dark, believing it Otsū; the victim is Akakabe Yasoma.
Takuan and temple watchmen find Otsū unconscious but alive near the marsh.
Takuan confronts Osugi; Osugi and Matahachi flee the scene.
Musashi spends about four days as Kōetsu and Myōshū's guest, observing art and craft.
Ōtaguro and Yoshioka messengers deliver Denshichirō's challenge for nine at night at Rengeōin.
Kōetsu and Shōyū take Musashi to the Ōgiya in Yanagimachi.
Musashi's blank-paper response reaches Yoshino while she entertains Karasumaru's courtly party off-page.
Musashi quietly leaves the Ōgiya intending to keep the duel appointment at Rengeōin.
Musashi walks through snowy Shijō, the Kamo crossing and Gion woods to Rengeōin.
Denshichirō waits with Ōtaguro and Yoshioka retainers; Musashi appears from the veranda after warming himself.
Musashi detects the ambush and kills Ōtaguro before the main duel.
Musashi kills Denshichirō with his sword.
Genzaemon and the disciples search while Musashi hides under the eaves and escapes from the north side.
Shōyū confronts Karasumaru and Konoe over access to Yoshino; Takuan referees their game.
Musashi returns from Rengeōin and reunites with Takuan at the Ōgiya.
The party moves into Yoshino's rustic cottage behind the pleasure house.
Yoshino wipes Denshichirō's blood from Musashi's sleeve and calls the stain a peony petal.
The hearth party composes verse and Yoshino plays the biwa.
Word arrives that Yoshioka men have surrounded the quarter, preventing Musashi's safe departure.
Alone with Musashi, Yoshino diagnoses his spiritual rigidity and breaks open the biwa to reveal its varied inner structure.
Musashi and Yoshino acknowledge mutual attraction, but the text does not establish a sexual union.
Otsū lies feverish and unable to eat at Karasumaru's residence while Jōtarō cares for her.
Takuan returns from Daitokuji after receiving news that his mother is seriously ill.
Takuan entrusts Otsū and Jōtarō to Karasumaru, then departs intending to reach his seriously ill mother in Tajima.
Takuan tells Jōtarō that Musashi is at the Ōgiya with Yoshino.
Jōtarō angrily sets out intending to find Yanagimachi and the Ōgiya; Otsū remains ill at Karasumaru's residence.
Jōtarō enters the Ōgiya and injures a servant with his wooden sword; the servant later survives.
An attendant leads Jōtarō to Musashi in Yoshino's cottage.
Musashi learns the Yoshioka blockade; Kōetsu sends old clothes and a note for disguise.
Unable to reach busy Yoshino directly, Musashi receives her scented aloeswood note from Rin’ya.
Musashi and Jōtarō approach the main gate in disguise.
Yoshioka men surround the disguised Musashi and Jōtarō at the Yanagimachi gate.
Kojirō prevents an illegal street melee and invokes magistrate Itakura's authority.
A public duel is set for five the morning after next at the spreading pine; child Genjirō is named Yoshioka representative with disciples as seconds.
Musashi and Jōtarō separate at the Yanagi Riding Grounds after escaping the crowd.
At Karasumaru's rear gate Musashi refuses to visit sick Otsū before the likely fatal duel and leaves Jōtarō a message.
Otsū comes outside and finds Jōtarō crying after Musashi's departure.
Matahachi tells Osugi that Musashi's Ichijōji duel is the next morning.
Akemi tells Matahachi that Okō ran away with Gion Tōji.
Akemi takes Osugi's travel money, leaves a note and flees the inn.
Around two in the morning Osugi and Matahachi leave with a drawn map, intending to reach Ichijōji.
Before dawn roughly seventy Yoshioka men deploy on three roads with bows and a musket around the spreading pine.
Kojirō arrives as an observer and clashes verbally with the Yoshioka group.
Kojirō supplies a hostile account of Musashi's past and tactical habits.
Kojirō whispers an additional trick intended to ensure Musashi arrives; the text withholds its content.
After meditating at Kurama, Musashi returns to a small inn north of Kitano, buys food and new underclothes, and prepares.
Musashi learns from a coffin-maker that his uncle Matsuo Kaname has died.
At the Upper Kamo crossing Kojirō warns Musashi about the Yoshioka numbers; Musashi insists on going alone.
Otsū and Jōtarō encounter Musashi on the mountain route; the ill Otsū coughs blood and receives water and support.
Musashi and Otsū explicitly confess their love while discussing death and discipline.
Musashi leaves Otsū and Jōtarō and continues toward Ichijōji; arrival is not shown in this chapter.
Osugi and Matahachi lose their way near Mount Daimonji while trying to reach Ichijōji.
Matahachi finds Akemi below the cliff; her scream was caused by Jōtarō's Nara mask.
Matahachi persuades Akemi to abandon her Musashi search and travel east with him.
Matahachi chooses Akemi and leaves Osugi alone on the mountain.
Kojirō reaches the spreading pine and takes an elevated observer's position.
Musashi approaches by a difficult detour and purifies himself at a shrine basin without entrusting the outcome to a deity.
Musashi disables the musketeer's fuse with a thrown stone.
Musashi deliberately attacks the symbolic head and kills child Genjirō by decapitation.
Musashi kills Miike and multiple unnamed Yoshioka men; Kobashi is struck, but the chapter does not establish Kobashi's death.
Musashi sustains wounds to his knee and forearm during the mass fight.
Under pressure Musashi instinctively fights with two swords, later conceptualized as a method against a large force.
Musashi escapes along the Shugakuin path through barley fields and woods as the pursuit disperses.
Musashi recuperates for ten days at Mudōji with the acolyte Seinen.
Musashi carves a sandalwood Kannon as a penitential offering for Genjirō.
Sannōin and Enryakuji authorities condemn the killing of a child and order Musashi off the mountain.
Osugi infiltrates Mudōji at night and attacks Musashi; he throws and disarms her.
Musashi nurses the injured and feverish Osugi despite her hostility.
The temple supplies a cow for the planned descent toward Ōtsu; Musashi and the ill Osugi remain at Mudōji at chapter end.
Musashi escorts Osugi and the cow down past Miidera toward Ōmi.
After secretly drinking fresh milk, Osugi abandons Musashi and escapes toward Sakamoto or Ōtsu.
Musashi gives a country woman a letter for Otsū via Karasumaru, asking Otsū to meet at Seta's Kara Bridge.
At a pass inn Musashi and Matahachi meet for the first time since Sekigahara.
Akemi, who had traveled with Matahachi, has already left the inn with their belongings and money.
Musashi urges Matahachi to begin again, seek learning and join the journey to Edo.
Musashi sends Matahachi to find Osugi and meet him at Seta's Kara Bridge.
Kojirō arrives with three Mount Hiei priests, disparages Musashi to stonecutters, then discovers Musashi overheard him; their future rivalry is acknowledged.
At the Hermitage of the Mountain Moon, Otsū and Jōtarō receive Musashi's letter.
Otsū and Jōtarō leave via Shiga Pass for the Seta rendezvous.
Musashi rents the cow onward at Uchidegahama and continues to Seta.
Musashi reunites with Otsū and Jōtarō at the Kara Bridge tea shop during a storm.
Musashi plans an eastward life: Edo, education for Otsū and training for Jōtarō.
Matahachi is diverted into an unidentified brothel by Kojirō, becomes drunk and misses the Seta rendezvous.
The next day Matahachi follows the Nakasendō through Kusatsu, Hikone, Toriimoto and Suribachi Pass toward Nakatsugawa.
Outside Nakatsugawa Matahachi sees Otsū riding the cow with Musashi's party and turns resentfully against Musashi.
The eastbound group pauses near Magome Pass at the Male and Female Waterfalls.
Questioning Otsū about Matahachi, Musashi forcefully embraces and throws her down; she rejects him and flees.
Otsū regrets the pain caused by her rejection and returns toward the waterfall area.
Musashi stands under the male waterfall to purge desire and renew discipline; the act is not presented as suicide.
Otsū waits in the hut with Musashi's kimono and swords while Jōtarō understands that the journey has entered a serious pause.
